notes:
Summary: QuickForge builds an IDE-first copilot embedded in their Electron-based devbox and web IDE. Primary ask: predictable low-latency streaming for token-at-a-time completions and tight token budget control to avoid UI jank and runaway token costs. They care about TTFT (time-to-first-token) and 95th%-tile jitter under real dev workloads.

Key requirements / constraints:
- TTFT target: <= 70ms on local devbox (within NA region) for <128 token completions.
- 95th %-tile jitter goal: <30ms across typical workday traffic bursts.
- Throughput: many concurrent devboxes (target 800 active users peak per cluster) with bursty typing patterns.
- Token budget controls: per-session token caps, soft warnings, and automatic shorter-fallback models when budget hit.
- Backpressure behavior: prefer partial streaming + immediate UI patching rather than blocking until full chunk; must support incremental edits and cancel semantics.
- Model/version pinning: want ability to pin stable model for GA users and canary newer model for beta. Must support fast rollback.
- Security: VPC endpoint + SAML SSO for internal users; audit logs and KMS integration required.

What we discussed on calls:
- "If the first token is delayed we get a very visible typing stutter — needs to feel instantaneous." — Lead UX PM
- SE notes: local latency dominated by devbox-to-region network; smart routing to nearest edge + reduced prefill size improves TTFT.
- They asked about automatic token budget tuning: Redwood Optimize suggestions for per-workspace quantization + batching rules.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2026-02-25: Intro call + product fit — agreed to scoped POC focused on TTFT (ff_2026-02-25_arch_review).
- 2026-03-03: Demo of streaming API + model variants; discussed pinning and rollback. (ff_2026-03-03_qf_demo).
- 2026-03-05: Security questionnaire submitted; Redwood provided SOC2/architectural notes and initial network checklist. (SEC-1187).
- 2026-03-09: SE workshop — synthetic devbox load test plan created, agreed success criteria (TTFT <=70ms, 95p jitter <30ms).
- 2026-03-11: Pricing request for Dedicated 12-mo commit; AE sent draft.

POC scope (short):
- 48h sustained run on Redwood Dedicated dev cluster configured with streaming enabled, prefix caching on, KV cache warming, and two model variants (fast low-token model + quality fallback).
- Collect TTFT, per-token latency histogram, 95th jitter, and failure modes under backpressure.
- Exercise token-budget logic: soft cap alert, auto-fallback to shorter model, and cancel semantics from IDE.

Open questions / risks:
- Whether prefix/KV caching will be effective for small interactive completions originating from local snippets. SE to validate caching hit rate.
- Network egress rules on their corporate firewall may introduce unpredictable latency — need NAT/proxy config.
- POC budget limited to 48h — may need extended run to capture typical diurnal burst patterns.

Next actions (assigned):
- Daniel Park to deploy POC config and provide k8s / routing manifest examples (due 2026-03-14).
- QuickForge infra to provision SAML test account and open firewall for Dedicated cluster IPs (owner: QuickForge SRE).
- Ava to finalize Dedicated 12-mo pricing and include token-band discounts.

Sales notes / positioning:
- Emphasize Redwood's streaming optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache, attention kernel selection) and routing policies to meet TTFT.
- Offer Optimize runbook for token budget tuning and automated recommendations.
- Prepare template rollback/playbook for model pinning and canarying to reduce release risk.

Quoted soundbite from QuickForge Lead Eng: "We need the copilot to feel like it's typing with the dev — not waiting for a response."
